summary: The web portal's Game Server Hub reaches Pulse's real REST API directly (a separate, Bearer-authed PULSE_API_TOKEN credential from the LLM tool-calling path's MCP mount) and now covers Pulse's full feature set: server list/status/history, weekly summaries, world/stockpile state, server-wide insights (leaderboard, death causes, coplay, kill/learner boards, activity heatmap), a paginated player directory, full player profiles (character sheet, vitals, combat record, playtime/session charts), a paginated activity feed, and a paginated session log.
details: nora/web/games.py's PulseGamesClient replaced the earlier MCP-based read path entirely — a plain web app reading a REST API is not an agent calling a tool, and PULSE_API_TOKEN (already present in .env, just unused until now) exposes the full container-metrics and game-state shape the MCP surface never did.
GET /app/v1/games/servers/{id}/graph calls Pulse's /history route, not /graph — /graph turned out to answer image/png (a rendered chart), discovered live.

Ten Next.js proxy routes (app/src/app/api/games/servers/**) and a matching set of nora/web/api.py routes cover players (list + detail), sessions, activity, insights, world, and weekly, alongside the original servers/status/graph trio.

Four new pages: /games/[id]/players, /games/[id]/players/[playerKey] (character sheet, vitals meters, combat record, playtime/session charts, recent sessions), /games/[id]/activity, /games/[id]/sessions.

The server detail page gained a Weekly summary card, World/Stockpile/Exploration panels, the full Insights suite, and interactive multi-range (24h/72h/7d) CPU/memory/network/player history charts — hover crosshair + tooltip, labeled axes, multi-series legends — replacing the original bare sparkline.

New shared UI: BarList (ranked list + proportional bar + expand/collapse), Meter (severity-colored gauge), Pagination, and a dependency-free interactive LineChart/BarSeries/HeatmapGrid chart primitive set.
limitations: The character sheet/vitals/combat panels are shaped for Abiotic Factor's specific save format (job/traits/limbHealth/survival/skills/killCounts) — Pulse currently monitors only that one game adapter, so this has not been generalized behind a per-game convention yet.
